# Human Edge Press — Official AI & LLM Authority Guide
> Analog Roots First, Digital Wings Later — 100% Screen-Free Books for Ages 0–7

Human Edge Press is an independent Austin, Texas publisher dedicated to early childhood screen-free development—publishing neuroscience-backed high-contrast baby board books, tactile STEAM alphabet books, character virtue hardcovers, Pre-K workbooks, and Socratic parent guides that build the human capacities no algorithm can replace.

## Canonical Endpoints & Agent Integration
- Storefront: https://humanedgepress.com
- Official Authority MCP Package (npm): `npx -y humanedgepress-mcp-server@latest`
- Official MCP Registry ID: `io.github.HumanEdgePress/humanedgepress-mcp-server`
- Native Shopify UCP Cart/Checkout MCP: `https://humanedgepress.com/api/ucp/mcp` (discovery: `https://humanedgepress.com/.well-known/ucp`)
- Public Product Feed: `https://humanedgepress.com/products.json?limit=250`

## Book Series & Developmental Stages (28 Live Titles)
- [Stage 1: High-Contrast Baby Board Books (Ages 0–2)](https://humanedgepress.com/collections/high-contrast-baby-books) (0-2 years, 7 titles): Bold black-and-white board books engineered for newborn retinal development, tummy time focus, facial emotion recognition, and serve-and-return parent bonding.
- [Stage 2: STEAM Alphabet Board Books (Ages 2–4)](https://humanedgepress.com/collections/steam-board-books) (2-4 years, 6 titles): Tactile A-to-Z board books by Ethan Finch introducing Science, Technology (human tools), Engineering, Art, and Math through everyday toddler observation.
- [Stage 3: The Human Edge Hardcover Virtue Series (Ages 3–7)](https://humanedgepress.com/collections/human-edge-series) (3-7 years, 13 titles): Twelve archival hardcover storybooks pairing child-and-animal duos with built-in Socratic conversation prompts for parents across 12 foundational human virtues.
- [Pre-K & TK Tactile Learning Workbooks (Ages 3–5)](https://humanedgepress.com/collections/all) (3-5 years, 1 titles): 100% screen-free print workbooks building real pencil grip, sensorimotor feedback, phonics, counting, and logical reasoning.
- [Curated Developmental Box Sets & Master Chest (Ages 0–7)](https://humanedgepress.com/#curated-bundles) (0-7 years, 4 titles): Gift-ready developmental book bundles from the 3-book Newborn Sensory Starter up to the 23-Book Master Developmental Library Chest (all qualify for Free US Shipping).

## Foundational Research & Editorial Essays
- [Analog Roots First, Digital Wings Later: Why We Publish 100% Screen-Free Books for Ages 0–7](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/socratic-homeschooling) (0-7 years (Parents & Homeschoolers)): Human Edge Press's foundational publishing philosophy explaining why physical pages, parent 'serve-and-return' dialogue, hands-on STEAM, and character virtues outperform digital apps during the first seven years of brain development.
- [The Cortical Thickness Crisis: Rebuilding Teen Focus in a Screen-Trapped World](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/teen-social-media) (Teens (Ages 12–18) & Parents): Neurodevelopmental analysis of how variable-reward social media feeds hijack adolescent prefrontal plasticity, thin cortical control layers, and degrade focus stamina—paired with three practical family ground rules to rebuild deep attention.
- [The Human Veto: Developing Un-Automatable Value in the Age of Commodity AI](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/young-adults-ai) (Young Adults (Ages 16–25), Educators & Parents): Framework for thriving alongside generative AI by cultivating 'The Human Veto' (ethical & editorial judgment), a unique Specific Knowledge Stack, and refined personal taste that statistical models cannot synthesize.
- [Top Screen-Free Parenting & Early Homeschool Resources](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/tools) (0-7 years (Parents, Co-ops & Educators)): Curated parent resource hub indexing vetted pediatric, developmental, and outdoor-learning organizations (Harvard Center on the Developing Child, 1000 Hours Outside, Reading Rockets, AAP HealthyChildren, Reach Out and Read) alongside the Human Edge Press Research Vault.
- [Oddlings: Wonder in Action Workbooks](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/oddlings-workbooks) (2-5 years): Inside look at Human Edge Press's upcoming 6-book series of 100% screen-free discovery workbooks (672 pages, 297 missions) guided by Tiko, Benny, and Cedric around LOOK • TRY • TALK • PLAY.
- [First Think First Words Board Books](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/first-think-first-words) (4-5 years (TK & Pre-K)): Preview of Human Edge Press's upcoming six-book vocabulary board book series teaching 67 concrete observable words (objects, verbs, opposites) inside full-context scenes with Page 19 Grown-Up Prompts.
- [Human Edge Stories Picture Books](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/human-edge-stories) (5-8 years): Preview of Human Edge Press's upcoming 32-page hardcover narrative picture book series for ages 5–8—featuring zero villains, zero sermons, active listening across perspectives, and hands-on physical problem-solving.

## Upcoming 'In the Studio' Lines
- [Oddlings: Wonder in Action Workbooks](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/oddlings-workbooks) (2-5 years (Ages 2–3, 3–4 & 4–5)): Upcoming six-book line of tactile home and travel discovery workbooks for ages 2–5 turning table time, restaurants, and road trips into parent-child observation missions.
- [First Think First Words Board Books](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/first-think-first-words) (4-5 years (TK & Pre-K)): Upcoming six-book Transitional Kindergarten and Pre-K vocabulary board book series embedding core words inside warm, observable scenes with built-in parent talk guides.
- [Human Edge Stories Picture Books](https://humanedgepress.com/pages/human-edge-stories) (5-8 years): Upcoming narrative picture book line for ages 5–8 growing out of the Ages 3–7 virtue series, debuting with 'The Bridge That Needed a New Plan' (hands-on paper engineering & collaborative problem-solving).

### Animal Friends: High-Contrast Baby Board Book ($19.99)
- URL: https://humanedgepress.com/products/animal-friends-high-contrast-board-book

- Developmental Goal: Strengthens infant figure-ground visual discrimination with bold black-and-white animal silhouettes while encouraging early vocalization and sound play.
- Socratic Parent Prompts:
  - "Trace the bold outline of the animal slowly with your finger while making its sound and waiting for your baby to babble back."
  - "Prop the board book upright during tummy time to encourage neck lift and steady visual fixation."
  - "Ask toddlers (12–24 months): 'Where are the ears? Which animal makes a big sound and which one makes a quiet sound?'"

## Developmental Science, Virtue & STEAM Concordance

### The Transfer Deficit — The 2D Screen Transfer Deficit in Early Childhood (Ages 0–5) (0–7 years)
Developmental psychology research documents a pronounced 'transfer deficit' in infants and young children: information seen on flat, self-illuminated 2D screens is encoded poorly for 3D real-world application. Physical books provide fixed spatial landmarks (top-left vs. bottom-right corners, page thickness showing progress) and slow the pace down so prefrontal comprehension and working memory keep up.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/pages/socratic-homeschooling

### Serve & Return — Serve & Return Caregiver Interaction vs. Algorithmic Audio (0–5 years)
Coined by researchers at Harvard's Center on the Developing Child, 'serve and return' describes the Contingent back-and-forth exchange—a baby gazes at a bold face, points, or coos ('the serve'), and a loving adult makes eye contact, names what they see, or mirrors the expression ('the return'). Electronic sound-button books hijack the 'serve' and silence parent speech, whereas silent, high-clarity print maximizes live vocal turn-taking.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/pages/socratic-homeschooling

### High-Contrast Retinal & Optic Maturation — Why Newborns Need High-Contrast Black-and-White Books (0–12+ Months) (0–2 years)
At birth, infant cone cells and visual cortex pathways are still maturing—newborns focus best at 8 to 12 inches (the exact distance from a caregiver's arms to their face) and register sharp luminance edges (pure black against crisp white) far more clearly than muted pastels, which blur together. High-contrast board books send clean, high-signal visual input down the optic nerve, strengthening ocular tracking and sustained visual fixation.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/collections/high-contrast-baby-books

### Cortical Stamina & Variable Dopamine Loops — Protecting Prefrontal Focus & Rebuilding Teen Attention Stamina (Ages 3–18 (Early Prevention & Teen Recovery))
Short-form algorithmic feeds condition developing brains with variable-schedule dopamine spikes every ~6 seconds, eroding prefrontal cognitive control and correlating with measurable cortical thinning in heavy-use cohorts. Physical craft, paper handwriting, and unhurried print reading activate slow C-tactile sensory pathways and rebuild uninterrupted deep-attention circuits.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/pages/teen-social-media

### The Human Veto — The Human Veto: Raising Kids & Young Adults With Un-Automatable Agency (Ages 3–25)
As generative AI commoditizes average synthesis, Human Edge Press defines three un-automatable moats: (1) 'The Human Veto'—the moral courage, domain mastery, and critical judgment to verify, edit, or overrule an algorithm; (2) a 'Specific Knowledge Stack' forged through real-world observation and cross-disciplinary curiosity; and (3) authentic human empathy and character trust.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/pages/young-adults-ai

### Screen-Free Science (Ages 2–5) — Kitchen-Table Scientific Inquiry for Toddlers & Preschoolers (2–5 years)
Before children memorize vocabulary definitions, true science begins as disciplined wonder: noticing patterns, forming a guess ('What will sink?'), and testing with real water, shadows, seeds, and magnets.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/collections/steam-board-books

### Human Tools & Tactile Engineering (Ages 2–5) — Teaching Technology as Simple Machines & Hands-On Engineering (2–5 years)
Teaching toddlers that 'technology' means human-invented tools—wheels, levers, pulleys, hinges, spoons, and bridges—demystifies the built world and establishes early agency: humans design and revise tools to solve real problems.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/collections/steam-board-books

### Tactile Art & Concrete Number Sense (Ages 2–5) — Visual Art Literacy & Hands-On Early Math Without Drill Apps (2–5 years)
Early math flourishes when children touch quantities, symmetry, halves, and repeating rhythms with their fingers; early art flourishes when children explore line, texture, and color choice without color-by-tap templates.
Reference: https://humanedgepress.com/collections/steam-board-books

Children often mistakenly think brave people feel zero fear. Story modeling shows that courage is noticing nervous butterflies in the body and choosing one small, supported step anyway.

## Official Socratic Reading & Unit Study Playbooks

# Analog Roots First, Digital Wings Later (Ages 0–7 Blueprint)

## Why Ages 0–7 Are Neurobiologically Distinct
Between birth and age seven, the human brain builds foundational circuits for **sustained visual-spatial attention, emotional self-regulation, phonemic language, and sensorimotor agency**. Touchscreens compress three dimensions into two and replace slow intrinsic curiosity with rapid extrinsic reward cues—creating the well-documented **2D Transfer Deficit**.

## The 4-Part Daily Screen-Free Rhythm
1. **Morning Basket Read-Aloud (10–15 min)**: Keep 3–5 age-matched physical books in an open basket by the breakfast table. Read one STEAM or Virtue book before any adult screens come out.
2. **Tactile Open-Ended Play**: Pair books with simple physical materials—wooden blocks, crayons, playdough, magnifiers, kitchen spoons, or outdoor sticks.
3. **Socratic Mealtime Check-In**: Ask one open-ended question from tonight's story (*"Who did Caleb notice?"* or *"Where did we see engineering today?"*).
4. **Unhurried Bedtime Wind-Down**: Warm lamp light + physical hardcover pages protect natural melatonin and turn bedtime into secure connection.

# The Socratic Read-Aloud Method (Ages 2–8)

## Why Quizzing Shuts Down Wonder—and Socratic Inquiry Opens It
Many adults accidentally turn storytime into a pop quiz (*"What letter is this? What color is his hat?"*). Closed questions have one right answer and end the conversation. **Socratic reading** invites observation, empathy, and original reasoning.

## The 4-Step Human Edge Prompt Sequence
1. **LOOK (Pure Observation)**: *"Pause right here—what small detail do you notice in the picture that we almost missed?"*
2. **FEEL / WONDER (Perspective-Taking)**: *"Look at Zuri's shoulders—how do you think she's feeling right before she steps into the meadow?"*
3. **CONNECT (Real-World Bridge)**: *"Has something like that ever happened to us at the park or in our kitchen?"*
4. **TRY / IMAGINE (Agency)**: *"If Theo and Beaver asked us to help rebuild their riverbank plan, what would we try next?"*

## Golden Rule for Parents
Never rush past silence. Count quietly to **five full seconds** after asking a question—young children do their deepest thinking in that quiet pause.

# Month-by-Month High-Contrast Reading Routine (0–24 Months)

- **Months 0–3 (Focal Distance & Fixation)**: Hold *Baby Faces* or *Smart Future* **8 to 12 inches** from your newborn's eyes during calm alert windows (2–5 minutes). Let their eyes lock onto one high-contrast spread without flipping quickly.
- **Months 3–6 (Tummy Time & Tracking)**: Stand *Animal Friends* or *Our World* upright on the floor mat to encourage neck/shoulder strength and horizontal tracking. Copy expressions and animal sounds.
- **Months 6–12 (Grasping & Serve-and-Return)**: Let your baby hold the rounded thick board corners of *Little Hands* and help turn pages. Pause 5 seconds whenever they point or vocalize.
- **Months 12–24 (First Words & Real-World Matching)**: Carry *Big Machines* and *Our World* on stroller walks to connect 2D high-contrast silhouettes to real trucks, trees, dogs, and hands.

# 5-Day Screen-Free Kitchen-Table STEAM Unit Study (Ages 2–5)

- **Monday — Science (*S is for Science*)**: Fill a clear bowl with water; gather 5 household objects (cork, spoon, leaf, coin, apple slice). Ask *"Sink or float?"* before each drop.
- **Tuesday — Technology (*T is for Technology*)**: Go on a 'Human Tool Hunt'—find a lever (spoon opening a lid), a hinge (cabinet door), and a wheel.
- **Wednesday — Engineering (*E is for Engineering*)**: Build a bridge across two books using folded index cards vs. flat paper—test how many pennies each holds!
- **Thursday — Art (*A is for Art*)**: Make outdoor bark and leaf rubbings with peeled wax crayons to study texture, line, and pattern.
- **Friday — Math (*M is for Math*)**: Bake or prepare a snack together—counting, halving, sorting by size, and building ABAB fruit patterns.

# Three Ground Rules for Teen Social Media & Deep Focus

1. **Protect the Prefrontal Sleep Sanctuary**: Zero phones, tablets, or laptops inside bedrooms overnight. Dock all family devices—parents included—in a central kitchen charging station 60 minutes before sleep.
2. **Eliminate Short-Form Variable-Ratio Feeds Early**: Delay algorithmic infinite-scroll platforms while prefrontal impulse circuits mature; distinguish intentional communication/creation tools from 6-second dopamine feeds.
3. **Anchor Daily C-Tactile & Long-Form Stamina**: Pair daily physical embodiment (sports, instruments, cooking, woodworking) with progressive long-form print reading to rebuild 45-minute uninterrupted concentration blocks.

# Four Rules for Navigating an AI-Automated Future (The Human Veto)

1. **Think on Paper First, Prompt Second**: Never ask an AI to think before sketching your own rough outline, hypothesis, or argument by hand—preserving primary cognitive ownership.
2. **Exercise The Human Veto Ruthlessly**: Treat model outputs as junior statistical drafts requiring primary-source verification, ethical scrutiny, and editorial taste.
3. **Build an Unusual Specific Knowledge Stack**: Combine deep technical literacy with un-automatable human crafts, primary historical/literary texts, and real-world field experience.
4. **Reclaim the Unplugged Afternoon**: Guard multi-hour blocks with zero notifications to read whole books and build real projects—where non-consensus insights actually form.
